Salmonella Warning Issued for Eggs Imported from Ukraine
The UK Food Standards Agency (FSA) has
issued
an urgent food safety warning after eggs imported from Ukraine were found to contain
Salmonella
Enteritidis, urging consumers not to eat the affected products and businesses to withdraw them from sale.
Kyiv-based poultry company Yasensvit Ltd supplied the contaminated eggs and are primarily sold through small retailers, wholesalers, caterers and food manufacturers rather than major supermarket chains.
The warning applies to all pack sizes and best-before dates bearing the producer code 3UA1012066.
The eggs were identified during sampling conducted as part of an investigation into a Salmonella outbreak. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) had initially been investigating an outbreak involving a different strain of the bacteria. However, Salmonella Enteritidis has been linked to 36 cases reported in England this year.
Jacqueline McCormick, head of incidents at the FSA, said the agency had taken urgent action to protect public health, calling on businesses to withdraw affected products and recall them where they had already been sold to consumers.
She stressed that eggs produced in the UK were not affected by the warning.
The FSA advised consumers not to eat the contaminated eggs and urged businesses to follow its official food safety alert. It added that eggs not covered by the warning should remain safe when thoroughly cooked and handled hygienically.
However, infants, young children, pregnant people and older adults should only consume raw or lightly cooked eggs carrying the British Lion mark or produced under the Laid in Britain scheme, according to the agency.
The FSA said it would continue working with UKHSA and other partners as the investigation progresses.
